# Streamlit

A Python framework that renders a script top-to-bottom as a web app, re-running the whole script on
every interaction. In [[labour-fraud-analysis]] it is the **anomaly console** — 219 lines in
`src/app.py`, launched by `make app`, and the surface where the investigation's four signals are
meant to be read.

## Shape of the app

- `st.set_page_config(layout="wide")`, then a hand-written HTML title block through
  `st.markdown(unsafe_allow_html=True)` — the framework's default chrome overridden rather than
  accepted.
- `@st.cache_data` on a single loader that reads every CSV in `data/csv` into a dict of frames. The
  cache is what makes the re-run-everything model affordable: twenty tables parse once, not once per
  click. See [[pandas]].
- A five-metric row via `st.columns(5)` — people, companies, permits, documents, total structured
  rows — every one computed as a `len()` rather than typed in.
- `st.tabs(["Overview", "Anomaly dashboard", "Entity network", "Finances", "Documents"])`. The
  anomaly tab is the analytical core; the network tab renders the [[networkx]] graph;
  the documents tab is the [[chain-of-custody]] surface.
- One `style(fig)` helper applied to every plotly figure, holding the whole palette in five module
  constants. A single styling function is what keeps a five-tab dashboard looking like one artefact.

## The disclosure banner is part of the app, not the README

`st.info` renders a synthetic-data notice on the page itself, above the first chart. Someone who
arrives at a screenshot or a shared browser tab, having never opened the repository, still sees the
disclosure. That is [[provenance-and-limits-stated-inline]] applied to a running UI, and it is the
right place for it given [[synthesise-rather-than-redact]].

## What it costs, and the deliberate second door

Streamlit needs a Python process, a port, and twelve pip packages. It cannot be emailed, cannot be
opened from a USB stick, and cannot be handed to a reviewer who does not run Python. That is exactly
why the same twenty tables are also served by a hand-written vanilla-JS viewer with all libraries
vendored and no build step — [[offline-first-static-deliverable]] and
[[zero-dependency-no-build-step]] — and by a notebook that CI executes end-to-end
([[reproducible-analysis]]).

Three surfaces over one dataset is a real cost: the four signals are implemented three times, and
the bulk-permit threshold is hard-coded identically in all of them plus the test suite.
